items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: there was a fellow named John Ephrat, and he conceived the idea of starting a Broadway softball league

ctx.x: I heard you also got a little baseball in in your career. You were with a pit band?

Yeah. All the theaters, there was a fellow named John Ephrat, and he conceived the idea of starting a Broadway softball league, and all the theaters would have a ball team and they would compete with each other. And this meant that anybody in the cast or the stage hands could be a member of the team, which produced some pretty shabby ball teams. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-

There were some of them that were pretty good but most of them were pretty low key. And I was with “Silk Stockings,” the Cole Porter show. And we won the championship that year. And I played ball when I was a kid, we played ball, had a neighborhood ball team. And my dad and my two uncles, my father’s two brothers were very good ball players. We played baseball. So I had started out a long time ago playing ball and I enjoyed it, and we had a lot of fun out there. It was fun.
